proof.text: Localize the canonical integral pullback/tensor isomorphism. The chosen rational pullback and tensor functors have the integral object formulas specified by their existsUnique characterizations. Conjugate the localized isomorphism by these object equalities. conj_eqToHom_iff_heq gives the required equality of homs; Iso.ext gives uniqueness. The other existing normalization, compatibility, and descent theorems remain named proof obligations in this module with their existing source proofs in their docstrings.

Import the unchanged comparison-counit theorem and the canonical integral constructor from the extracted integral construction module. That module proves the tensor and two pullback counit invertibilities and constructs the original conjugated coherent-limit comparison; the assigned module re-exports these declarations.

For pullbackTensorFiniteGood, use the normalized algebraic lift of proEtaleModuleInverseImage and its equal-universe presentation. The pro-etale topos has a conservative family of points, and each point admits the ringed-site presentation. AlgebraicInverseImageOfUniverses.isKFlat_of_points therefore preserves K-flatness under the inverse-image part, with no flatness assumption on individual terms. Apply changeOfRings_isKFlat_independentCoefficients to the recorded scalar-extension functor and constant-ring comparison. Its objects and maps are the actual tensor construction, so this gives K-flatness for the tensor-coordinate pullback. Finally map openSquarePullbackModel termwise and tensor its component with an arbitrary acyclic test complex. Acyclicity transports through that isomorphism, giving the intrinsic finite pullback criterion. This argument also applies to the empty scheme, zero complex and first quotient.

For pullbackTensorQuotient_existsUnique, apply finiteQuotientPullbackDescent directly to pullbackTensorQuotientComplex and the already proved finite K-flat preservation theorem. Its normalization square is definitionally the existing pullbackTensorQuotientNormalization predicate. The full descent proof is in a separate proved helper module to avoid rechecking expanded functor expressions in this already large module. No representative, counit, quotient functor, statement or proof obligation is changed.

Import the coherent reduction and strict tower realization declarations from CompletedPullbackTowerRealizations, preserving their original signatures and constructions. This compile-time extraction retains all existing normalization obligations under the same declaration names. The main module publicly re-exports them and the extracted integral construction supplies the original private sequence-ring equality for the remaining import-all consumer.

For pullbackTensorQuotientOrdinary_existsUnique, reuse the proved quotient ring square and sectionwise-identity direct-image/scalar-restriction comparison in StrictScalarPullbackComparison. Compose sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction at m with the normalized quotient adjunction at X, and compose the quotient adjunction at Y with sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction at n. Transport the latter right adjoint by the direct-image comparison, then apply leftAdjointUniq. The existing scalar_comparison_unit calculation gives the required section equation. For uniqueness, use injectivity of the first composite adjunction Hom equivalence. Its component formula, the sectionwise identity of the right-adjoint comparison, and the two normalized quotient units turn any candidate section equation into equality with the transported composite unit. Sheaf, natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality conclude. No K-flatness or quotient-flatness assumption is needed; the same proof includes n=m.

For canonicalRationalPullbackTensor_scalar, apply target scalar localization to canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor_scalar on the underlying integral objects. The prescribed object formulas identify all six vertices. The normalization of canonicalRationalPullbackTensor identifies each comparison hom with its localized integral hom. The rational pullback and scalar-extension pure-tensor formulas at coefficient one, and the rational tensor bilinear formula at the pair of coefficients one, identify all functor images. Transport these identifications through dependent applications, product morphisms and composition using heterogeneous equality. The two rational composites are therefore the localizations of the equal integral composites. This proves the unchanged rational scalar square without a new proof obligation.

For canonicalFinitePullbackTensor_quotient, express the two composites as natural transformations on the product of finite derived categories, using finitePullbackTensorConstructionIso, the quotient tensorators and the uniquely normalized quotient/pullback comparison. Flat-term K-flat resolutions provide representative isomorphisms for both inputs. Apply finitePullbackTensor_quotient_representatives to the existing unit-normalized ordinary comparison and its cochain extension; its degree equation is reflexive and its derived counit square is precisely the existing existsUnique specification. Naturality along the pair of resolution isomorphisms and cancellation extend equality to all inputs. Evaluate the natural-transformation equality at (M,N). This is a decomposition: the strictly narrower representative calculation remains a named obligation in a new module.

For the integral scalar square, take three inputs (M,N,M) and good K-flat representatives using essential surjectivity of integralOperationsGoodLocalization. Apply completedComparisonQuotientNormalization at (identity_X,f) to obtain good expressions and invertible substitutions. completedComparisonCanonicalIdentification identifies the E strict comparison transport with the prescribed canonical integral comparison. completedComparisonScalarLimitImage identifies the L strict comparison transport and gives both completed scalar composites as the same conjugated total-limit arrow. Choose the strict left route, rewrite the two canonical identifications, and compose the two equalities. Full-subcategory hom extensionality gives the original scalar square. No new proof obligation is introduced.

Publicly import the extracted coherent construction module. It contains the original normalized finite evaluation and coherent evaluation, associativity, braiding and unit proofs; the quotient descent uses its existing proved private resolving-isomorphism naturality helper through import all. This changes no comparison or proof obligation and keeps the profiled parent file within the compile limit.

theorem canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor_scalar {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [hX : ∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [hY : ∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (M N : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y) :
    (sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
      E L ι X).map ((@canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor l _ E _ _ _ X Y f hX hY) M N).hom ≫
      (integralTensorScalarComparison l E L ι X
        (((@constructibleIntegralPullback l _ E _ _ _ X Y f hX hY)).obj M)
        (((@constructibleIntegralPullback l _ E _ _ _ X Y f hX hY)).obj N)).hom ≫
      ((@constructibleIntegralTensor l _ L _ _ _ X hX)).map
        (Prod.mkHom (integralPullbackScalarComparison l E L ι f M).hom
          (integralPullbackScalarComparison l E L ι f N).hom) =
    (integralPullbackScalarComparison l E L ι f
      (((@constructibleIntegralTensor l _ E _ _ _ Y hY)).obj (M,N))).hom ≫
      ((@constructibleIntegralPullback l _ L _ _ _ X Y f hX hY)).map
        (integralTensorScalarComparison l E L ι Y M N).hom ≫
      ((@canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor l _ L _ _ _ X Y f hX hY)
        ((sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l
          (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) E L ι Y).obj M)
        ((sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l
          (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) E L ι Y).obj N)).hom
